rules.lines:
Normalize first, as markdown-it 15 does (core rule normalize): every "
" and every lone "" becomes "
", and every NUL becomes U+FFFD. Then split at "
". So "
", "
" and a lone "" each end a line; depths, costs, cut lines and notice line numbers count these lines.
rules.markers: A line's prefix is its longest leading run of spaces, tabs and container markers. A container marker is ">", or a list marker ("-", "+", "*", or 1 to 9 digits and "." or ")") followed by a space, a tab or the line end. m = the markers in the prefix; w = the spaces and tabs in the prefix, in columns, also those before the first marker and after the last; a tab runs to the next stop of 4, columns counted from the line start with each marker character one column.
rules.depth: A non-blank line's own depth is m + floor(w / 2). A blank line (empty, or only spaces and tabs) takes the depth of the line before it. A line right after a blank line, and the first line, takes its own depth; a line right after a non-blank line takes the larger of its own depth and that line's depth. A long line counts as depth 0 for the line after it.
rules.cost: Each line costs (D + 1) x (2 + its UTF-8 bytes, after normalizing). The work is the sum. The budget is 16,000,000; a case's cut is the first line (from 0) where the running sum passes it, or null.
rules.limits: Each case gives its own limits; lineBytes null means no line rule. A notice with rule "net" never appears in these cases.
rules.budget: Where the running sum passes limits.budget, that line and every line after it are one top-level paragraph, whitespace collapsed; the lines before it are read as a document. One notice: rule "budget", its first line (from 1) and how many lines it cut.
rules.long: With limits.lineBytes set, a non-blank line of more than lineBytes UTF-8 bytes is never parsed: it costs its bytes once, it is one top-level paragraph as typed, the text before it is read as a document and the text after it is read afresh; the line after it takes its own depth, as after a blank line. One notice for all such lines before the budget cut: rule "line", the first one's line (from 1) and how many there are.
rules.fence: A fence is tracked from a line, not in a fence and not long, whose text after its prefix starts with 3 or more "`" with no "`" after them, or 3 or more "~". The opener's containers are its prefix's markers. Each later line first walks those containers: for a ">", any spaces and tabs then the ">"; for a list item, spaces and tabs up to its least content column (its marker's end plus one, in columns from the line start); a line that lacks a ">" or has text before that column leaves them, and the fence ends there. Otherwise a line that is not long ends the fence when, after the containers, it has any spaces and tabs, at least as many of the opener's character, then only spaces and tabs. When a long line sits in a tracked fence, the text after it starts with the fence's opening line again, charged once more at that line's own depth (m + floor(w / 2)), so the code stays code.
